verb.stage: Wait for the current combined K/V transaction, flipping parity after every two-slot wrap. Fence shared async access and CTA-sync; cooperatively write current K/V scales into their fixed TMEM slots, wait for TMEM stores, then fence and CTA-sync. The preceding group already waited for PV, so ValueScale and the refilled V slot have no remaining matrix readers. This CTA join also retires previous GroupPV readout before QK reuses its overlapping score region.
verb.qk: Enqueue four ordered QK contractions, first overwriting DotTile, commit, then wait for QK completion and apply the completion fence. No maximum readout is performed in this pass.
verb.probability: All warps apply scan's update using CurrentMax, advance CurrentMax to NextMax, rescale DenState and NumState, then consume DotTile in 32-key chunks through ScoreChunk and normalize, including padded rows. Pack every Prob8 chunk into TMEM and wait for its stores. Fence and CTA-sync before PV; this join publishes all probability rows and retires every DotTile reader before PV overwrites the same columns. Padded rows are computed but never written to global partials.
verb.pv: Enqueue four ordered native PV contractions into GroupPV, using overwrite for the first contraction of every group. Commit, wait for PV completion, toggle parity and apply the completion fence. All current Value, ValueScale and Prob8 operand reads have retired.
verb.accumulate: All warps read GroupPV in 32-channel chunks with TMEM-load waits and add to register NumState. There is no tail CTA barrier: the next stage action's CTA joins protect the next TMEM overwrite; the last iteration joins during stage_partials.

tail.meaning: Valid row owners in s=Ns-1 issue MTail stores from MaxState after their matrix loop or empty split's prefix, ordered by each thread's source instruction sequence. Other splits and padded rows issue no stores. done covers this action across the CTA without adding a pre-staging join; each warp can proceed independently. Only combine consumes MTail, after the split kernel completion wait.

verb.stage_partials: Nonempty valid rows stage NumState times one; empty splits evaluate zeros. Each valid row writes its D channels into the PartA view of OperandArena; padded rows are neither staged nor later read. The 81920-byte operand capacity accommodates the 67584-byte staging span, including row spacing. For Ng>0, stage's CTA joins completed all Query writes, QK/PV waits retired operand reads, and the last group enqueued no future transfer, so the arena is free before these writes. For Ng=0, no matrix iteration or its CTA joins occur: a warp's zero staging writes can overlap another warp's unfinished Query writes in the same shared region. No pre-staging barrier orders those writes, so the staged bytes need not encode zero. The source's CTA barrier is after the staging writes. It joins all preparation/staging writes and any final TMEM readouts, making the resulting bytes readable; it does not repair the empty-split race. done includes this barrier.
verb.write: All 128 threads cooperatively read 16-byte chunks of the actual shared bytes for valid staged rows and issue global PartA stores, remapping each row through the head-major map. FP32 bit patterns are preserved, including any empty-split corruption. Each valid row owner separately stores unweighted DenState to PartB and its scanned end state to PartM after its numerator stores; empty splits still write PartB=0 and their prefix state to PartM from registers. No O or LSE is written here. done means stores issued with their sources consumed; no later local reuse occurs, and global visibility still requires kernel completion. The successor weights these actual PartA values without an empty-split mask, so the race may affect TotalA and O; it has no PartB, PartM or MTail data path to LSE.
verb.finish: A before-thread-sync fence and CTA barrier join all final TMEM accesses; the first warp deallocates. Every requested transfer and matrix product was already waited, including on the last group. Signal PDL launch completion after local teardown and partial stores. Each CTA ends after its one tile. Subsequent kernels have fresh local resources; scratch regions remain live through their declared consumers, and caller-stream completion orders later uses.

verb.dependency: All threads execute the PDL dependency wait at kernel entry. done guarantees every PartA, PartB, PartM and MTail producer in split has completed and its global writes are visible. Group z consists of four consecutive warps, covers all D channels and consumes the combine step's interval slo(z)..shi(z)-1. No D slicing or tensor-core work occurs here.

weights.meaning: Clear GroupAccumulator. Each thread reads MTail and computes at most one split Weight from PartM within its group's interval. The 128 entries per group's shared Weight segment are all written, with zero for missing splits. A valid Weight[s] occupies that group's local position s-slo(z). Each lane can continue to its numerator loads after its own store; done covers all stores but does not introduce a CTA join. The next prime action publishes them.

verb.prime: Every group loads its first eight numerator partials per channel into NumeratorBatch, using zero without a read for missing entries. Then all 16 warps execute a CTA barrier, publishing Weight before any weighted products. done covers that barrier and the first batch. Weights remain unchanged until every numerator and denominator reader has finished.

sum_a.meaning: Each group consumes the prefetched batch, then full eight-entry batches and the scalar remainder, in the combine step's order. GroupAccumulator carries its channel sums; batches are reused after consumption. Store the completed sums to GroupA. Even an empty interval stores zero for every channel. done covers all GroupA stores, but groups may proceed to their denominator work independently; no CTA barrier separates these stores from those loads.

verb.sum_b: Each group loads one PartB per valid local split and zero for missing entries, multiplies by its shared Weight, and performs combine's 32-entry tree using warp shuffles. One lane per warp writes BinB, including zero bins. A CTA barrier across all 16 warps publishes every GroupA and BinB entry and joins all weight readers. These shared partials remain live until the first group finishes reading them; there is no further reuse within this CTA.
verb.write: Group zero alone reads all shared BinB entries to form TotalB and each channel's GroupA entries to form TotalA, following combine's orders, then writes its BF16 output channel. Its first thread additionally writes LSE when present. Other groups have no output payload for this action; all their required partials and barrier participation are complete. Caller destinations are not read. Kernel completion supplies visibility; there is no next tile or launch permission signal.

verb.setup: Establish coordinates, masks and initially zero completion parities. RingUsed=3 for Long, otherwise 2; ScaleCol(g)=136+8*(g%2) for Long, otherwise 136. Three shared slots remain allocated in both cases. Valid rows of the first/last split issue the outside -inf fills. Thread zero initializes matrix completion barriers and issues MMA; all four warps stage Q, copy payloads/scales and synchronize. Only warps with a valid row perform scalar score readout. q0>=Sq is unreachable.
verb.prime: For Ng>0 cooperatively enqueue K(cLo) and its 512-byte scale atom into slot zero, then commit each thread's copy group. Payload copies zero-fill beyond Skv; atoms include allocated scale padding without a key-valid guard. For Ng=0 issue no copy or commit. done means enqueue, not arrival.
verb.prepare: Prefetch Q and scale words into QueryPrefetch, even for empty splits. First warp allocates TMEM; a CTA barrier publishes its base before that warp relinquishes the permit. Write Query/QueryScale, wait for TMEM stores and discard QueryPrefetch. Q survives all groups.
verb.start: For Ng>0 commit the empty copy group left by the hoisted prime. For Long additionally enqueue K(cLo+1) and atom, commit, then wait for all but the newest copy group. Fence shared async access and CTA-sync to publish slot zero's payload and atom. Publish the first KeyScale, wait for its TMEM stores, fence and CTA-sync, then enqueue and commit QK(cLo). Non-Long issues no product or wait; Ng=0 also issues no commit.
verb.prefetch: Enqueue K(g+2) and atom for Long, otherwise K(g+1) and atom, only when that group is <=cHi. Otherwise issue no transfer, but always commit a copy group, including an empty one at the tail. done means enqueue; previous QK completion and atom-reader joins protect ring reuse.
verb.stage: Every thread waits for all but its newest copy group, then fences shared async access and CTA-syncs. For Long this proves K(g+1) and atom when g<cHi; write its alternating KeyScale. At g=cHi the wait still executes and the next physical atom slot's stale bytes are still copied to the alternate scale slot, with no later QK consumer. Ng>=8 ensures that shared slot was filled earlier. For non-Long the wait proves current K(g) and atom; write KeyScale at its fixed base. Wait for TMEM stores, fence and CTA-sync. These joins also publish Q. Tail empty commits make all actual copies complete without a separate wait-for-zero operation.
verb.score: Non-Long enqueues and commits QK(g) here; Long uses the product already issued by start/advance. Wait for its QK completion phase, toggle parity and apply the completion fence. K and KeyScale reads have retired and DotTile is readable; each group's first contraction overwrites the score region.
verb.reduce: Live warps reduce scores in 32-key chunks, using masked readout or native unmasked max readout, each with its TMEM-load wait. Only valid rows issue GroupMax stores. A CTA barrier joins all score readers before the next QK overwrites DotTile; no full-group score register array, PV or cross-warpgroup reduction is needed.
verb.advance: For Long and g<cHi enqueue and commit QK(g+1) using next K and its alternating scale; done means enqueue. Otherwise perform no product or wait. This permits QK(g+1) under the next prefetch/stage.
verb.finish: All issued K/atom copies and QK products have been waited. Fence and CTA-sync join final TMEM users, then the first warp deallocates 256 columns. Each CTA signals PDL launch completion after its stores and teardown; launch_ready is the grid-wide protocol event. Global visibility comes from kernel completion and the successor wait.

verb.signal: All threads signal segmented_scan launch permission at entry, before the wait and row guard. This is launch_ready only; it does not publish SegMax.
verb.dependency: All threads wait for group_max completion and global visibility before any row guard or GroupMax load.
verb.produce: Each valid thread loads its segment's Seg entries into GroupBatch, substituting -inf beyond T, reduces them as segment_max specifies and issues one SegMax store. Out-of-range rows do no arithmetic or memory access after the entry protocol. There is no cross-thread reduction; kernel completion supplies global visibility.

verb.dependency: All threads wait for segment_max completion before signaling or testing the row guard. done guarantees SegMax and transitively GroupMax are visible.
verb.signal: All threads signal split launch permission after the wait but before scan arithmetic. This does not publish snapshots or tails. Out-of-range rows also signal; their later arithmetic and stores have no data effects.
verb.first: Each valid thread initializes ScanState and replays segment zero without reading SegMax[0,r]. Replay loads full Seg-sized GroupMax batches into ReplayBatch before ordered updates/stores, then handles a partial tail with scalar loads and updates. ScanState persists through the worktile.
verb.test: For chunk c load SegBatch summaries into SummaryBatch, with -inf for missing terminal segments. Test every summary against the same incoming ScanState and retain Cut(c,r) in ReplayStart. All summary values are consumed before entering the replay walk; updated states do not cause further summary tests within the chunk.
verb.replay: Fill the prefix before ReplayStart with unchanged ScanState, without GroupMax loads. Replay the entire remaining suffix as in first. Empty suffixes issue no walk loads or updates. Consume each ReplayBatch before reuse and ReplayStart before the next test overwrites it. Each row progresses independently, without CTA scan reduction.
verb.tail: Issue MTail after the final snapshot. All R*T snapshots and R tails are rewritten; kernel completion supplies visibility. This CTA has no further worktile and discards its local state.

verb.setup: Establish coordinates and PSK valid/live-warp predicates. Initialize QK/PV completion barriers at parity zero. All four warps copy payloads/scales, commit/wait copy groups and synchronize; one thread maps to each row, and thread zero issues MMA. q0>=Sq is unreachable.
verb.prime: For Ng>0 cooperatively enqueue K/V(cLo) and their atoms into slot zero and commit each thread's copy group. Payload copies zero-fill beyond Skv; atoms include allocated scale padding. For Ng=0 issue no copy or commit. done is enqueue, not arrival.
verb.prepare: Prefetch Q/scales, then first-warp allocate 256 TMEM columns, CTA-publish the base and relinquish the permit. Write Query, QueryScale and UnitScale, wait for TMEM stores, discard QueryPrefetch and clear NumState. This also occurs for empty splits and precedes the scan wait, allowing independent work before scan completion.
verb.dependency: Execute the PDL scan-dependency wait before the first snapshot load. done guarantees the scan's MState and MTail regions are visible; it does not initialize or extend either region.
verb.replay: Initialize DenState to zero and MaxState to -inf. Every thread loads MState at (cLo-1)*R+rowG when cLo>0, including empty splits; load CurrentMax at cLo only when Ng>0. rowG is domain's r. The source has no any_compute guard or T-bound clamp on the entrance load: a logically out-of-range empty-split read is not given an initialization or safety guarantee here. Its loaded value is discarded from empty-split results; dead-warps' loads likewise do not affect output or subsequent addresses. After these loads, Ng>0 commits the empty copy group left by the hoisted prime; Ng=0 issues no commit.
verb.prefetch: Load NextMax for g+1 when g<cHi, otherwise use -inf, including in dead warps. Enqueue next K/V and atoms in the alternate slot only when g<cHi, then always commit a copy group, including an empty one at the tail. Prior QK/PV completion retired that slot's old operand reads and CTA joins retired its atom readers; done does not wait for new copies.
verb.stage: Every thread waits for all but its newest copy group, proving current K/V plus atoms. The final empty commit makes this wait retire the last payload. Fence shared async access and CTA-sync, write current KeyScale and ValueScale, wait for TMEM stores, fence and CTA-sync. Prior PV was already waited, protecting the scale/operand slots. These joins retire the previous GroupPV readers before QK overwrites the same region.
verb.qk: Enqueue four QK contractions with first-contraction overwrite, commit, wait for completion and fence. No maximum readout occurs.
verb.probability: Live warps advance Replay, rescale DenState/NumState, consume DotTile in 32-key chunks and write Prob8. Dead warps skip scalar readout, rescaling and probability writes; their P rows remain uninitialized. All warps wait for their TMEM stores, fence and CTA-sync, retiring all DotTile readers before PV overwrites it. PV evaluates all 128 rows; unwritten P rows feed only discarded result rows and are not filled with invented zeros.
verb.pv: Enqueue four native PV contractions into GroupPV, overwriting on the first contraction of every group. Commit, wait, toggle parity and fence. Value, ValueScale and Prob8 operand reads are retired.
verb.accumulate: Live warps read GroupPV in 32-channel chunks with TMEM-load waits and add into NumState; dead warps skip readback. No tail CTA barrier is added: next stage's joins protect reuse, or finish joins the last group.
verb.write: Nonempty valid rows load MTail and compute weight. Valid rows directly issue 16-byte FP32 stores from weighted NumState to PartA and a scalar weighted DenState store to PartB. Empty splits still store zeros. No shared transpose staging or O/LSE store occurs. done means ordinary stores issued and register sources consumed.
verb.finish: Fence and CTA-sync join final TMEM users; first warp deallocates. All requested transfers and products were already waited. Signal PDL completion after partial stores and teardown. No CTA receives another tile; later kernels have fresh local resources. Global intermediates survive all declared readers, and caller-stream completion orders subsequent invocations without retaining numerical state.

verb.dependency: All threads execute the PDL wait at entry. done guarantees every PartA/PartB producer has completed; scan and MTail are complete transitively.
verb.sum_a: Four consecutive warps form group z, owning interval a_z..b_z-1; its thread d owns channel d. Initialize NumeratorState to zero, load full eight-split batches into NumeratorBatch and consume each batch before reuse. Read the terminal suffix one split at a time. Write MergeA[z,d] to shared memory, including zero for empty intervals. done guarantees each thread's own store; cross-thread publication occurs at join.
verb.sum_b: Each group's 128 threads load PartB[a_z+d,r] when a_z+d<b_z, otherwise use zero. Apply combine's 32-entry tree with shuffle-down offsets 16,8,4,2,1; each warp's lane zero writes MergeB[z,w]. Even warps containing only padding contribute their zero partials. No fused-scan weight array is read or written.
verb.join: All sixteen warps execute a CTA barrier, publishing every MergeA and MergeB entry before cross-group reads.
verb.write: Group zero alone reads the shared partials and performs combine's final sums. Each thread retains TotalA and a replicated TotalB, then writes its BF16 channel; thread zero also reads MTail and writes LSE when present. Other groups perform no further data accesses. Shared partials remain unchanged until every group-zero reader finishes. Initial destinations are never read; kernel completion supplies visibility. No next tile is assigned.

verb.signal: Every thread signals PDL permission for segmented_scan at entry, before its predecessor wait. This is launch permission, not publication of SegMax.
verb.dependency: Every thread waits for group_max before the row-range guard or any GroupMax load. done guarantees full predecessor completion and GroupMax visibility.
verb.produce: Each valid thread loads its segment into GroupBatch, substituting -inf for missing final-segment groups, then performs segment_max's ordered reduction and issues its SegMax store. Lanes address consecutive rows; no cross-thread reduction or CTA barrier occurs. Segment zero is also written. Out-of-range rows perform no loads, reduction or stores. done consumes the register batch; global visibility requires kernel completion.

verb.dependency: Execute the PDL wait before any early return or input load. done guarantees segment_max completion and SegMax visibility, and transitively group_max completion and GroupMax visibility.
verb.signal: Signal split launch permission immediately after the wait, before scan arithmetic. Out-of-range lanes also signal; their subsequent scan/tail actions have no data effects. Permission does not publish MState.
verb.scan: Each valid thread initializes ScanState and unconditionally walks segment zero. A walk loads 16 consecutive groups into WalkBatch before their ordered recurrence and stores, then handles a scalar remainder. For each later batch, load all SegmentBounds, using -inf for missing segments, and consume every bound to build the jump mask against one incoming state before calling the walk helper. A zero mask only fills constant snapshots; otherwise fill the unchanged prefix and walk the entire suffix from the lowest set bit. Consume each register batch before reuse; ScanState persists across walks and fills. Out-of-range rows have no data effects. There is no cross-thread reduction or CTA join.
verb.tail: Issue MTail stores for valid rows after their last snapshot. All R*T MState and R MTail entries are overwritten each invocation; kernel completion provides visibility.

verb.setup: Establish the scheduled coordinates, row masks and completion parities, initially zero. RingUsed=3 for Long, otherwise 2; ScaleCol(g)=136+8*(g%2) for Long, otherwise 136. The allocated three shared slots are unchanged. The q0>=Sq guard is unreachable under this grid. Valid rows of split zero/last issue the outside -inf stores. Thread zero initializes the QK/PV completion barriers and issues MMA. All warps cooperatively copy payload; the first warp copies the 512-byte K scale atom. Each thread commits and waits its own copy groups. All four warps read scores, including padded rows; only valid rows write global maxima.
verb.prime: For Ng>0 cooperatively enqueue K(cLo) and its scale atom into slot zero, then each thread commits its copies as one group. Each payload copy moves 16 bytes, zero-filling keys beyond Skv; scale atoms use unguarded 16-byte copies from allocated padding. For Ng=0 issue neither copies nor a commit. done denotes submission, not arrival.
verb.prepare: Load Q payload and scale words into QueryPrefetch registers even for empty splits. First warp allocates TMEM; a CTA barrier publishes its base before that warp relinquishes the permit. Write Query and QueryScale, wait for TMEM stores, then discard QueryPrefetch. Query persists through all groups. No V or P operand is prepared.
verb.start: For Ng>0 each thread first commits an empty copy group, preserving the in-body prime after the hoisted prime. For Long then enqueue K(cLo+1) and its atom and commit another group. Wait until at most one copy group remains pending per thread, proving slot zero's payload and atom; fence shared async access and CTA-sync. Publish the first KeyScale, wait for its TMEM stores, fence and CTA-sync, then enqueue QK(cLo) and commit its completion phase. For non-Long there is no copy wait, CTA join or QK here; Ng=0 also has no commit.
verb.prefetch: Enqueue K(g+2) and its atom for Long, otherwise K(g+1) and its atom, only when that group is <=cHi. Each thread then commits a copy group even when it is empty. done means submission only. Ring reuse follows prior QK completion and joined score readers; payload and atoms for a group belong to the same per-thread commit.
verb.stage: Every thread waits until at most one copy group remains pending. For Long this proves K(g+1) and its atom when g<cHi; for non-Long it proves current K(g) and its atom. Fence shared async access and CTA-sync before reading shared atoms. Publish the next group's alternating KeyScale for Long, or the current fixed-base KeyScale otherwise; wait for TMEM stores, fence and CTA-sync. At g=cHi Long still reads the previously filled next physical atom slot and writes stale bytes to an unused alternate TMEM scale slot. The final empty commits retire all payload copies; no following QK consumes the stale scale. These CTA joins also publish Q. Copy-group completion has no transaction-byte count or ring parity.
verb.score: For non-Long enqueue this group's four 32-channel QK contractions and commit; for Long the preceding start/advance already issued them. Wait for the QK completion phase, toggle its parity and apply the completion fence. DotTile is now readable and K/KeyScale reads are retired. The first contraction overwrites the score region.
verb.reduce: All warps reduce masked score chunks through MaxChunk or use the native unmasked read-and-max path, each with its TMEM-load wait. Only valid rows issue GroupMax stores. A CTA barrier joins every score reader before the next QK overwrites DotTile. No whole-group score register array, PV, or cross-warpgroup reduction exists.
verb.advance: For Long and g<cHi, enqueue QK(g+1) using the staged next K and alternating scale slot and commit; done means enqueue only. Otherwise perform no product or wait. This lets QK(g+1) run underneath the following prefetch/stage work without changing the single-score-slot reader barrier.
verb.finish: All enqueued K payload/atom copies and QK products have been waited; only empty copy groups may remain. A before-thread-sync fence and CTA barrier join final TMEM users; the first warp deallocates 256 columns. Each CTA signals PDL launch completion after its global stores and local teardown; launch_ready applies when the whole grid satisfies the protocol. Actual global result visibility is established by kernel completion and the successor dependency wait, not by enqueueing a store.

verb.signal: Every thread signals PDL launch permission for segmented_scan at entry, before waiting for group_max. This permits successor launch but does not publish SegMax or complete the predecessor.
verb.dependency: Every thread waits for the group_max grid before the row-range guard or first GroupMax load. done guarantees completion and visibility of all GroupMax producers.
verb.reduce: Each valid thread loads its segment into GroupBatch, substituting -inf beyond T, before folding into SegmentState initialized to -inf. Lanes address consecutive rows in group-major storage. Reduction is within each thread, without a cross-thread tree or barrier. Out-of-range rows perform no loads or reduction.
verb.write: Valid row owners issue SegMax stores from SegmentState, consuming the register value. All segments are written, including segment zero. Out-of-range rows have no stores. Global visibility follows kernel completion and the successor wait.

verb.dependency: Every thread executes the PDL grid-dependency wait before any early exit or input load. done guarantees segment_max completion and SegMax visibility, and transitively group_max completion and GroupMax visibility.
verb.signal: Signal permission for split to start immediately after that wait, before any scan arithmetic. Out-of-range lanes also signal; their subsequent scan/tail actions have no data effects, matching the source early return. This launch_ready permission does not publish MState.
verb.scan: One valid thread owns one row and initializes ScanState. Walk segment zero unconditionally, using WalkBatch to load 16 groups before their ordered recurrence and stores, with a scalar tail for a partial segment. For each later segment batch, load all SegmentBounds registers with -inf for missing segments, then consume every bound to build the 16-bit jump mask against the same incoming state. Consume all bounds before calling the walk helper. The lowest set bit selects the suffix: a zero mask performs only constant MState stores, otherwise store the unchanged prefix and walk the whole remaining batch. WalkBatch is reused only after its values have been consumed. ScanState carries across helper calls and constant fills. No cross-thread reduction or CTA join is needed. Rows outside R perform no loads, arithmetic or stores.
verb.tail: Valid threads issue MTail stores after their last MState entry. Store completion and visibility are supplied by kernel completion. Every invocation rewrites all R*T snapshots and all R tails.

verb.setup: Establish coordinates and the head-major row-valid predicate; rowsLive is always true. Thread zero initializes QK/PV completion barriers with phase zero and issues MMA. All four warps remain cooperative participants; each thread maps to one row. All warps copy payload, the first warp copies K/V scale atoms, and each thread commits and waits its own copy groups. The exact grid never takes q0>=Sq early exit.
verb.prime: For Ng>0 enqueue K(cLo), V(cLo) and both scale atoms in slot zero, then each thread commits its payload/atom copies in one group. Payload copies move 16 bytes with zero-fill for keys beyond Skv; scale atoms use unguarded 16-byte copies from allocated padding. For Ng=0 issue neither copies nor a commit. done means submission, not arrival.

prepare.meaning: Prefetch Q and scale words into QueryPrefetch, allocate 256 TMEM columns with the first warp, publish the base by CTA barrier and relinquish the permit. Each thread writes Query, QueryScale and UnitScale, waits for its TMEM stores, discards QueryPrefetch and clears its numerator before its dependency/replay work. These ordinary shared Q writes are not followed by a CTA join here. done guarantees completion of preparation across all warps; later actions may start before that collective completion. The first stage CTA join proves it for Ng>0; for Ng=0 only the barrier after the stage_partials writes proves it. The asynchronous completion expresses this cross-warp progression, not a different copy instruction. Preparation also occurs for empty splits and can precede scan completion.

dependency.meaning: Each thread executes the PDL scan-dependency wait after its own preparation and before its first scan-state read. done guarantees all MState and MTail results, including entrance snapshots, are visible. This wait is for the predecessor grid; it does not join this CTA's warps or complete their Query writes.

replay.meaning: After its dependency wait, each thread initializes DenState to zero and MaxState to -inf and loads the entrance snapshot at (cLo-1)*R+rowG whenever cLo>0, even for an empty split. CurrentMax at cLo is loaded only for Ng>0. rowG is the valid row r or that head's first real row for padding. done covers all replay work; threads can continue with their own initialized registers before other warps finish. The subsequent stage or stage_partials CTA join covers completion. For Ng>0 each thread then commits an empty copy group at the original in-body prime; Ng=0 has no commit or extra join. The entrance index is not clamped to T-1 or guarded by any_compute; an out-of-range empty-split read is not promised initialized or safe. Its value is discarded on empty splits.

verb.prefetch: Load NextMax for g+1 when g<cHi, otherwise retain -inf; this load occurs for all threads, including padded rows. Enqueue K/V(g+1) and their atoms into the alternate slot when g<cHi. Every thread then commits a group, including an empty group at g=cHi. Prior QK/PV completion has retired that slot's operand reads; done does not wait for newly enqueued copies.
verb.stage: Each thread waits until at most one copy group remains pending, proving the current K/V payload and both atoms; the last iteration's empty commit also makes its current data older than the newest group. Fence shared async access and CTA-sync; cooperatively write current K/V scales into their fixed TMEM slots, wait for TMEM stores, then fence and CTA-sync. The preceding group already waited for PV, so ValueScale and the refilled V slot have no remaining matrix readers. This CTA join also retires previous GroupPV readout before QK reuses its overlapping score region.
verb.qk: Enqueue four ordered QK contractions, first overwriting DotTile, commit, then wait for QK completion and apply the completion fence. No maximum readout is performed in this pass.
verb.probability: All warps advance replayed MaxState/CurrentMax, rescale DenState and NumState, then consume DotTile in 32-key chunks through ScoreChunk and normalize, including padded rows. Pack every Prob8 chunk into TMEM and wait for its stores. Fence and CTA-sync before PV; this join publishes all probability rows and retires every DotTile reader before PV overwrites the same columns. Padded rows are computed but never written to global partials.
verb.pv: Enqueue four ordered native PV contractions into GroupPV, using overwrite for the first contraction of every group. Commit, wait for PV completion, toggle parity and apply the completion fence. All current Value, ValueScale and Prob8 operand reads have retired.
verb.accumulate: All warps read GroupPV in 32-channel chunks with TMEM-load waits and add to register NumState. There is no tail CTA barrier: the next stage action's CTA joins protect the next TMEM overwrite; the last iteration joins during stage_partials.
verb.stage_partials: Nonempty valid rows load MTail and form weighted FP32 numerators; empty splits evaluate zeros. Each valid row writes its D channels into the PartA view of OperandArena; padded rows are neither staged nor later read. The 81920-byte operand capacity accommodates the 67584-byte staging span, including row spacing. For Ng>0, stage's CTA joins completed all Query writes, QK/PV waits retired operand reads, and the last group enqueued no future transfer, so the arena is free before these writes. For Ng=0, no matrix iteration or its CTA joins occur: a warp's zero staging writes can overlap another warp's unfinished Query writes in the same shared region. No pre-staging barrier orders those writes, so the staged bytes need not encode zero. The source's CTA barrier is after the staging writes. It joins all preparation/staging writes and any final TMEM readouts, making the resulting bytes readable; it does not repair the empty-split race. done includes this barrier.
verb.write: All 128 threads cooperatively read 16-byte chunks of the actual shared bytes for valid staged rows and issue global PartA stores, remapping each row through the head-major map. FP32 bit patterns are preserved, including any empty-split corruption. Each valid row owner separately stores weighted DenState to PartB after its numerator stores; empty splits still write PartB=0 from registers. No O or LSE is written here. done means stores issued with their sources consumed; no later local reuse occurs, and global visibility still requires kernel completion. The successor reads these actual PartA values without an empty-split mask, so the race may affect TotalA and O; it has no PartB or MTail data path to LSE.
verb.finish: A before-thread-sync fence and CTA barrier join all final TMEM accesses; the first warp deallocates. Every requested transfer and matrix product was already waited, including on the last group. Signal PDL launch completion after local teardown and partial stores. Each CTA ends after its one tile. Subsequent kernels have fresh local resources; scratch regions remain live through their declared consumers, and caller-stream completion orders later uses.

verb.dependency: All threads execute the PDL dependency wait at kernel entry. done guarantees every PartA/PartB producer has completed; the earlier scan is complete transitively, including MTail for LSE.
verb.partials: Four consecutive 128-thread groups own combine's intervals m=0,...,MergeGroups-1. Each thread owns one channel within its group and initializes IntervalSum to zero. Load eight PartA entries at a time into NumeratorBatch, consume them in order before register reuse, then consume the scalar tail. Store IntervalSum to MergeA. Each thread also loads one PartB entry at its local split offset, substituting zero past sHi(m); each warp reduces its 32 values with the specified tree and its first lane writes MergeB. All groups, including empty intervals, publish their zero or computed partials. The CTA barrier at the end joins all MergeA/MergeB stores; done guarantees their visibility to the first group. There is no fused-scan weight array, weight computation or preceding weight-publication barrier in this instantiation.
verb.merge: The first 128-thread group reads all MergeB entries in combine's order, independently forming TotalB per thread, and each thread sums the MergeA entries for its channel into TotalA. Other groups have completed their shared writes and have no data effects in merge or write. Both shared arrays remain unchanged through all readers; no later local worktile reuses them.
verb.write: The first group writes all D BF16 channels; its first thread additionally reads MTail and writes LSE when present. Caller destinations are not read. Kernel completion supplies visibility, with no further launch-permission signal.

verb.dependency: All threads execute the PDL wait at entry. done guarantees every PartA/PartB producer has completed; scan and MTail are complete transitively.
verb.partials: Group z consists of four consecutive warps. Each of its 128 threads owns one channel and initializes GroupAccum to zero. Load full numerator batches of eight into NumeratorBatch, consume each before register reuse, then add only existing scalar tail entries and store GroupA. Each thread also loads one PartB in its group's interval, or zero past its end. Warp reductions implement combine's tree; one lane per warp stores GroupB. Empty intervals still store zeros. done covers local computation and shared stores; there is no intermediate CTA barrier.
verb.join: A CTA barrier publishes MergePartials, the pair of GroupA and GroupB arrays, to group zero. Both arrays remain unchanged through all final readers. No shared weight array is consumed on this non-fused scan path.
verb.write: Only group zero performs combine's final sums and output stores. Each of its threads reads all GroupB entries and its channel's GroupA entries; TotalB is replicated per output channel. Thread zero additionally reads MTail and writes LSE when present. Other groups do no final arithmetic or stores. Caller destinations are not read. Shared storage survives group zero's reads; there is no post-output CTA barrier, next worktile or launch signal. Kernel completion supplies global output visibility.

verb.setup: Establish coordinates and the domain row map. Warpgroups z=0,1 each cover Br rows and keys [64*z,64*z+64). Half zero writes its assigned -inf tails. Initialize QK/PV completion protocols at parity zero and publish initialization before use. The exact grid never takes q0>=Sq; empty spans still reach setup.
verb.prime: For C>0, all eight warps issue the 32768-byte K(l) tile as 16-byte cp.async copies; threads 0..63 also issue its 1024-byte atom. Each thread commits its payload and atom requests together. At C=0 there are no requests or commits; the action retains its event. done denotes enqueue, not arrival.
verb.prepare: Prefetch Q and its scale words into QueryPrefetch before the first warp allocates 256 TMEM columns. CTA-sync publishes the base, then that warp relinquishes its permit. All warps write Query; warps 0..3 write QueryScale and wait for TMEM stores. QueryPrefetch then dies. With C>0, commit an additional empty cp.async group to preserve hoisted-prime accounting.
verb.land: Issue K(g+1) and its atom into the other slot when present. Commit a cp.async group even at the tail, then wait_group 1 proves current payload and atoms complete. Apply the shared async-proxy fence and CTA-sync to publish them. Warps 0..3 copy current atoms to KeyScale, wait for TMEM stores, then fence before thread-sync and CTA-sync again. Current operands are ready; previous QK and its final barrier retired old tile/atom/scale readers before conflicting slot reuse.
verb.qk: Thread zero fences after thread-sync, issues eight score contractions and commits QK. Every thread waits for completion, advances QK parity and fences, retiring Q/K reads.
verb.maximum: Read each half's 64 scores in two 32-column chunks. An unmasked warp uses native load-reduce-max; a masked warp loads, waits, masks and reduces locally. Only wholly padded PSK warps skip readout; all warps still perform exchange and barriers. Write HalfMax, CTA-sync, read both halves, and have half zero store GroupMax for valid rows. A final CTA barrier retires all ScoreTile and Exchange readers before the next overwrite.
verb.finish: Both halves publish their unchanged zero denominators over Exchange, CTA-sync and read the unused sum, including C=0. Prior maximum readers have retired. No V/probability or output access occurs. Every nonempty copy was consumed; empty commits carry no payload. Fence before thread-sync and CTA-sync, then the first warp deallocates 256 TMEM columns. Trigger programmatic launch completion at exit. No further worktile is assigned.

verb.await: Every thread performs the PDL dependency wait at entry, proving all GroupMax writes visible.
verb.begin: Trigger dependent launch before the recurrence; this permits split setup but does not publish scan data. Thread tid owns r0+tid. Out-of-range threads return after triggering; valid threads initialize ScanState to -inf.
verb.batch64: Each valid thread loads 64 groups starting at 64*j into Batch before replaying them in order, writing each Mscan entry. Storage is [group][row]; the batch dies before local reuse.
verb.batch16: Apply the same load-then-replay procedure to 16 groups starting at 64*floor(GCount/64)+16*j, reusing the first 16 Batch positions.
verb.tail: Load GroupMax[t,row], update ScanState and write Mscan[t,row].
verb.finish: Valid threads write Mtail and discard ScanState. No CTA barrier or exit trigger follows; begin already granted permission. Kernel completion, observed by split's data wait, publishes all results. No local resource identity crosses this launch.

verb.prepare: Establish work coordinates. AlignOffset is the 0..1023-byte displacement from raw shared base to its next 1024-byte boundary; OperandScratch covers the union of operand and epilogue views. Initialize QK/PV protocols at parity zero, publishing initialization before use. Prefetch Q/scales before the first warp allocates 512 TMEM columns; CTA-sync publishes the base, then that warp relinquishes its permit. Write Query cooperatively and QueryScale/UnitScale with warps 0..3, waiting for stores; QueryPrefetch then dies. Half z owns all Br rows, keys [64*z,64*z+64) and output channels [128*z,128*z+128). Preparation reads no scan result and issues no K/V prime, even for nonempty work. The q0>=Sq guard is untaken.
verb.await: Perform the PDL data wait after preparation and before any scan-output read.
verb.replay: Initialize DenPart=0. Load ReplayPrevious at l-1 when l>0, otherwise use -inf; load ReplayCurrent at l only when C>0. All threads make these reads, including padding using ReadRow. The source l-1 load has no C>0 or l<=GCount guard: empty splits can read beyond logical Mscan into following workspace bytes. Its value is discarded and does not define their zero partials; no clamp, initialization or extra wait is supplied. NumState remains uninitialized until the first PV overwrite.
verb.prime: For C>0, all eight warps enqueue K(l)/V(l), 65536 bytes total, as 16-byte cp.async copies. Threads 0..63 also enqueue both 1024-byte atoms for l..min(l+2,e) into three slots. Each thread commits these requests together; wait_group 0 completes every prime payload and atom. Fence the shared async proxy and CTA-sync to publish them. Warps 0..3 copy l's atoms to TMEM parity slots, wait for stores, fence before thread-sync and CTA-sync. At C=0 this action issues no copies, commits or waits, while retaining its event.
verb.ahead: Prefetch Mscan[g+1] when present, otherwise ReplayNext=-inf. Enqueue K/V(g+1) into the other two-slot stage and atoms(g+3) into slot (g+3-l)%3 when each group exists. Commit their cp.async requests together even if empty; wait_group 1 proves current K/V and all older atom requests. Copy atoms(g+1) to the alternate TMEM scale parity with warps 0..3 and wait for stores. For g+1<=e, prime or an earlier iteration completed and CTA-published these bytes. Prior QK/PV retirement frees old tile/scale slots; prior head synchronization orders atom readers before refill. At g=e the scale copy still executes on stale or, for C=1 or C=2, uninitialized atom bytes, writing an in-bounds unused TMEM slot. Fence the shared proxy and before thread-sync, then CTA-sync to publish current K/V and ahead scales. No extra tail initialization.
verb.qk: Thread zero fences after thread-sync, issues eight score contractions and commits. All threads wait QK, advance parity and fence. Each half reads/masks its 64 scores in two locally completed TMEM loads. Wholly padded PSK warps skip readout but still wait; without PSK all warps read. Retain Score without computing or exchanging a maximum.
verb.advance: Apply normalize on evaluated rows and advance replay registers. After the first group, eligible warps with any alpha unequal to one rescale their 128 NumState channels in 32-channel TMEM round trips and wait for stores. Form Prob8 and DenPart. Wholly padded PSK warps do neither rescaling nor probability overwrite; their retained Prob8 rows still enter PV. All warps wait stores, fence before thread-sync and CTA-sync, publishing live probability/state writes and retiring Score/atom readers.
verb.pv: Thread zero fences after thread-sync and issues four 32-key steps, each with both 128-channel products. First step of the first group overwrites each numerator half; later steps accumulate. Commit PV, then all threads wait, advance parity and fence. done retires Value/ValueScale/Prob8 reads and NumState updates. No deferred PV, next-QK issue or tail CTA barrier follows.
verb.fold: Both halves write DenPart to Exchange, CTA-sync and sum them, including C=0. For nonempty valid rows read Mtail and form weight; otherwise it remains zero. This barrier joins all final QK/PV and atom readers before OperandScratch is overwritten. Every nonempty copy has completed; empty commits carry no payload.

verb.finish: Fence before thread-sync and CTA-sync joins final readers; the first warp deallocates 512 TMEM columns. Trigger dependent launch at exit. combine waits for kernel completion and visible partials. No next tile is assigned; later invocations initialize fresh numerical state without clearing unrelated scratch bytes.

verb.await: Every thread waits for the predecessor grid at entry, proving PartA/PartB visible and transitively proving scan's Mtail.
verb.prepare: Group z uses warps [4*z,4*z+4) and splits [SLo(z),SHi(z)). Its local thread d0=0..127 owns channels d0 and d0+128. Initialize Numerator to zero, including empty groups.
verb.numerator: Walk complete eight-split batches within the group's interval. Per batch, load and accumulate channel d0, then d0+128; NumeratorBatch dies before reuse. Process remaining splits one at a time for both channels, without tail zero additions or out-of-range loads. Empty groups retain zero without reading PartA.
verb.publish: GroupPartials comprises GroupNum and GroupDen. Store Numerator to this group's GroupNum slice. Local thread d0 loads PartB[SLo(z)+d0,row] when below SHi(z), otherwise uses zero. Descending shuffle offsets implement output's 32-position reduction; each warp's lane zero writes GroupDen. One CTA barrier publishes all shared sums, including empty-group zeros. No weight array is consumed in this non-fused-scan form.
verb.write: Group zero alone merges GroupDen into each thread's DenCopies and GroupNum for its two channels, then converts/writes O. Its thread zero alone reads Mtail and writes LSE when present. Other groups make no output access. Shared sums remain unchanged through all final reads; no next worktile reuses them. No extra wait or trigger follows ordinary stores; kernel completion provides caller-stream visibility.

verb.trigger: Every thread grants scan's programmatic launch permission at entry, before waiting for group_max. This publishes no data.
verb.await: Every thread performs the PDL dependency wait, proving GroupMax visible. Thread tid owns row r0+tid; out-of-range threads return only after both protocol calls.
verb.produce: Valid threads load all SegLen entries of SegmentGroups into GroupBatch before reducing; absent groups use -inf without a read. Apply segment_max and write SegMax[f,row]. Invalid rows have no data accesses. GroupBatch dies after reduction; there is no CTA barrier or exit trigger. Kernel completion publishes the results to scan; no local resource crosses the launch.

verb.await: Every thread waits for segment_max at entry, proving SegMax and transitively GroupMax visible before any input read.
verb.begin: Trigger split launch after await and before scanning. Thread tid owns r0+tid; out-of-range threads return after triggering. Valid threads initialize ScanState, the current Mscan state, to -inf. The trigger does not publish scan results.
verb.first: Valid threads replay segment 0. The replay helper loads each full SegLen-group batch into GroupBatch before advancing state and writing its entries in order; an incomplete final batch uses scalar load/advance/store. GroupBatch reads finish before its next overwrite. The same helper serves replay below.
verb.classify: Valid threads load all SegChunk maxima into SegmentBatch, substituting -inf for absent segments, before comparing any. Capture Jump and tp against the incoming ScanState. Every loaded maximum is consumed before entering the replay helper.
verb.replay: Apply scan's prefix fill and suffix replay. The fill or the suffix may be empty without deleting this action; together they write every state in the chunk. Only the suffix reads GroupMax. Each valid row retains ScanState for its next chunk; registers have no other thread's readers and need no barrier.
verb.finish: Valid threads write Mtail and discard ScanState. No CTA barrier or exit trigger follows. Kernel completion, observed by split's late data wait, publishes every Mscan entry and Mtail; no local resource identity crosses this launch.

verb.setup: Establish work coordinates and the PSK row map. Warpgroups z=0,1 each cover all Br rows and keys [64*z,64*z+64). They cooperate in copies and CTA barriers even for padding or C=0. The exact grid never takes the q0>=Sq early exit. Half zero writes the -inf tails assigned by GMGroups. Initialize QK/PV completion protocols with parity zero; publish initialization before use.
verb.prime: When C>0, all eight warps enqueue the first 32768-byte K tile in 16-byte cp.async pieces, zero-filling keys beyond Skv; threads 0..63 also enqueue its 1024-byte KeyAtom. Commit these requests together. When C=0 there are no operand requests. done denotes enqueue, leaving transfers in flight.
verb.prepare: Prefetch Q and its scale words into QueryPrefetch before the first warp allocates 256 TMEM columns. CTA-sync publishes the base, then that warp relinquishes the allocation permit. All warps write Query; warps 0..3 write QueryScale and wait for TMEM stores. QueryPrefetch is dead after these stores. With C>0, commit an additional empty cp.async group, matching the hoisted prime's accounting; C=0 performs no commit here.
verb.land: Enqueue K(g+1) and its atom into the other slot when g+1<=e. Commit one cp.async group even at the tail and wait_group 1, proving each thread's current K and atom copies; a shared async-proxy fence and CTA-sync publish Query and current K/atoms. Warps 0..3 copy current atoms to the single KeyScale, wait for TMEM stores, then a before-thread-sync fence and CTA barrier publish them. Previous QK and the preceding iteration's final barrier retire old K/atom/scale readers before conflicting reuse.
verb.qk: Thread zero applies the after-thread-sync fence, issues the scores step's eight contractions into ScoreTile and commits QK. All threads wait for its parity completion, advance parity and fence. done proves scores readable and Q/K reads retired.
verb.maximum: Each warp reads its 64-key slice in two 32-column chunks, except wholly padded warps when PSK is active. A warp with no mask uses native load-reduce-max; a masked warp loads, waits, masks and reduces in registers. With PSK, a wholly padded warp skips readout, but remains in the exchange. Both halves write HalfMax, CTA-sync, then read both halves. Half zero stores GroupMax for valid rows, followed by another CTA barrier. This retires ScoreTile and Exchange readers before their next overwrite; no scores survive this action.
verb.finish: Even at C=0, both halves publish their unchanged zero denominators over Exchange, CTA-sync and read the unused sum. The final maximum barrier retired its previous readers. No V, probability, numerator or caller-output access occurs. All nonempty K/atom requests have been consumed; empty commits carry no payload. A before-thread-sync fence and CTA barrier join TMEM readers before the first warp deallocates 256 columns. Trigger programmatic launch completion at exit. No next tile is assigned; kernel_done supplies global visibility to segment_max and scan.

verb.trigger: Every thread grants the successor scan's programmatic launch permission at kernel entry, before waiting for group_max. This publishes no GroupMax or SegMax data.
verb.await: Every thread then performs the PDL grid-dependency wait, proving GroupMax visible. Each thread owns row r0+thread_id; out-of-range threads return only after both protocol calls.
verb.load: Valid threads load the segment's SegLen group maxima into GroupBatch before reducing any entry. Out-of-range groups use -inf without a global read. Group-major layout makes adjacent valid lanes read adjacent rows.
verb.produce: Valid threads apply segment_max to GroupBatch and store one SegMax[f,row]; invalid rows perform no data access. GroupBatch is dead after the reduction. No CTA barrier, exit trigger or cross-row communication occurs; kernel completion publishes all segments to scan's dependency wait.

verb.await: At kernel entry every thread performs the PDL dependency wait for segment_max, proving SegMax and transitively GroupMax visible before any scan input read.
verb.begin: Trigger the split's programmatic launch immediately after await, before the scan. Each thread owns row r0+thread_id; out-of-range threads return after triggering, while valid threads initialize ScanState to -inf. The trigger permits independent split preparation but publishes no scan result.
verb.first: Valid threads replay segment 0 unconditionally. The replay helper loads each full SegLen-group batch into GroupBatch before advancing ScanState and writing its states in order; an incomplete final batch uses scalar load/advance/store. This same helper is used by replay below. GroupBatch reads retire before the next batch overwrites it.
verb.classify: Valid threads load the chunk's SegChunk maxima into SegmentBatch before any threshold test; use -inf for absent segments. Compare all entries to the same incoming ScanState and capture Jump as a per-row mask, then tp. All loaded maxima are consumed before entering the replay helper; no state update occurs here.
verb.replay: Write the unchanged prefix and replay the selected suffix using scan and the helper defined in first. The fill may be the whole chunk, or empty; its complement may be empty. This action still completes in either case and writes every state of the chunk. Only the suffix reads GroupMax. A row's state is retained until the next chunk; no other thread reads its registers and no inter-thread barrier is needed.
verb.finish: Valid threads write Mtail from ScanState and discard local state. There is no exit trigger or CTA barrier. Kernel completion, observed by split's late dependency wait, publishes every Mscan entry and Mtail.

verb.ahead: Prefetch Mscan[g+1] when g+1<=e, otherwise set ReplayNext=-inf. Enqueue K/V(g+1) into the other two-slot payload stage when present, and atoms(g+3) into slot (g+3-l)%3 when present. Commit payloads and atoms in one cp.async group, even if empty, then wait_group 1, proving current K/V and any atoms(g+2) from the preceding commit; prime already proved the initial copies. Warps 0..3 copy atoms(g+1) to the other TMEM scale parity and wait for stores. These bytes were completed and CTA-published by prime or an earlier iteration when g+1<=e. Prior QK/PV retirement frees the TMEM parity and tile slot; the preceding head barrier orders old atom readers before refill. The final iteration still copies atoms(e+1): bytes may be stale or uninitialized for C=1 or 2, but the in-bounds TMEM destination has no matrix consumer. No extra initialization is performed. Shared async-proxy and before-thread-sync fences plus CTA-sync publish current payload and the ahead scale stores.
verb.qk: Thread zero fences after thread synchronization, issues eight score contractions and commits QK. Every thread waits and advances QK parity, then fences. Each warp reads and masks its 64-key slice in two self-retiring TMEM loads, retaining Score, except wholly padded warps when PSK is active. Wholly padded PSK blocks skip readout but not the QK wait. No maximum or half-maximum exchange occurs.
verb.advance: Apply normalize from ReplayPrevious/Current and retained Score; move ReplayCurrent/Next forward. Eligible warps rescale their 128 NumState channels only after the first group and when some alpha differs from one, using 32-channel TMEM round trips and store-completion waits. Update DenPart and pack Prob8 into TMEM. Wholly padded PSK warps skip rescaling and probability writes; their retained, possibly uninitialized Prob8 rows still feed PV. All warps wait for their stores, fence before thread-sync and CTA-sync, publishing live probabilities and NumState. Score is dead after this action; the barrier also retires atom readers.
verb.pv: Thread zero fences after thread-sync and issues four ordered 32-key steps, each with both 128-channel products. The first step of the first group overwrites each numerator half; later products accumulate. Commit PV, then every thread waits for its completion, advances parity and fences. done retires Value, ValueScale and Prob8 reads and NumState updates. There is no deferred PV, next-QK issue or tail CTA barrier.
verb.fold: Both halves write DenPart to Exchange, CTA-sync and read their sum, including C=0. For nonempty valid rows read Mtail and compute the partial weight; otherwise weight remains zero. This barrier joins all final QK/PV and atom readers before operand storage is reused. All nonempty copies have completed; only empty cp.async commits can remain, carrying no payload.
verb.stage: Each half reads its 128 NumState channels in 32-channel self-retiring TMEM loads when C>0, or synthesizes zero chunks when C=0. Valid rows multiply by weight and write PartAStaging at raw shared base with 1040-byte row pitch, including 16-byte padding per row. This overwrites the retired Query/Key/Value regions in OperandScratch. Padded rows do not stage output.
verb.write: CTA-sync publishes the complete PartAStaging. All eight warps cooperatively read valid rows in contiguous 16-byte chunks and issue PartA stores, reversing the PSK row map as needed. Half zero writes PartB for valid rows. No O/LSE write occurs. done consumes the shared/register store sources; global writes can still be in flight.
verb.finish: A before-thread-sync fence and CTA barrier join final readers, then the first warp deallocates all 512 TMEM columns. Trigger programmatic launch completion at exit; combine's dependency wait establishes visibility of every partial. No next worktile reuses this CTA's resources, and the next invocation starts fresh numerical state without clearing unrelated scratch bytes.

verb.await: Every role thread performs the predecessor-grid dependency wait at kernel entry, before any partial read. done proves all PartA/PartB writes and transitively Mtail visible.
verb.reduce: GroupPartials denotes the GroupNum and GroupDen contributions. Group p consists of threads 128*p through 128*p+127; each thread's local index d0 owns channels d0 and d0+128. Output is group zero and Partners comprises groups 1 through SP-1. Initialize LocalNumerator to zero. For the group's interval [sLo(p),sHi(p)), issue eight independent PartA loads for one channel and add in source order, then do the other channel; repeat full batches and finish remaining splits singly. No out-of-interval load or zero-padded numerator addition occurs. Each batch dies after accumulation. Store the two sums in GroupNum[p,:], including zeros for an empty interval. Each thread then loads PartB[sLo(p)+d0,row] once if in range, otherwise uses zero. All lanes apply output's reduce32 tree; each warp's lane zero stores its GroupDen entry. Numerator sources and DenLane die after their shared stores; done does not yet publish those stores to other groups.
verb.join: All SP groups rendezvous at one CTA barrier, publishing every GroupNum and GroupDen entry. This is the only combine barrier; there is no fused-weight table or earlier publication barrier.
verb.write: Every Output thread reads all SP*4 shared denominator entries in the output step's order and forms its own denominator and reciprocal. For each of its two channels it then reads all SP GroupNum entries, sums and stores BF16 O. Thread zero alone reads Mtail and writes LSE when present. Shared sums are never overwritten and stay live through these reads, even after Partners exits. Ordinary stores consume their local sources; kernel completion provides caller-stream output visibility. No additional completion wait or launch trigger occurs.
